nodes.label: dragon-queue.ts
nodes.desc: Marigold's Queue (Tutorial Island · the Picky Dragon): the replay scene's state, read from the real timeline. One row per villager's chest, pouches counted one by one, Marigold's eye on the richest chest so far. Frames come only from the recording: a `read` of `accounts[k]` (or `totals[k]`) = chest k steps up; every change of the player's `total` = a pouch counted (editor line = the line that ran just before the change); after a chest's last pouch, one compare frame (did the player's `richest` change?). Vars on an event are the values BEFORE that line ran. The scene draws the code's own numbers, so a `total` that is never reset is drawn carried over (ember) and the caption says "Your code…"; the true chest sums only mark where it went wrong. Pure module (unit-tested); the component is components/replay/dragon-queue.tsx. Modes (from the case's arguments): "pick" = the boss (accounts → richest total), "list" = Quest 4 (accounts → the list of totals, no eye), "count" = Quest 2 (one chest), "shiny" = Quest 3 (given totals, the eye walks, no pouches).

Pure and seeded (same frames every time) so it can be unit-tested; components/fireworks.tsx draws the frames on a canvas and skips them entirely under reduced motion.

nodes.label: friends.ts
nodes.desc: Friends (C1): friend codes, requests and the shared shapes the store, API and friends book use. Rules (both stores enforce them): a request only goes out by friend code or link and needs the other player to accept; at most FRIEND_ATTEMPTS_PER_HOUR request attempts per player per hour (wrong codes count, so codes can't be guessed); at most MAX_FRIENDS friends plus outgoing requests.

nodes.label: game-types.ts
nodes.desc: Shapes shared by the page and its components.

nodes.label: goblin-cauldron.ts
nodes.desc: Grizzle's Cauldron (Tutorial Island · the Numerology Goblin): the replay scene's state, read from the real timeline. The number sits in the cauldron as digit tiles; the stew (the player's running `total`) sits below as chips, newest first, the way % 10 peels digits off the right. Line events carry vars as they were BEFORE the line ran, so a change seen at event i was made by the line that ran just before it. From those changes: - a number var (num / n) becoming itself // 10 is a SNIP (the peeked digit is the old value % 10); - `total` going up is an ADD to the stew; one digit frame = one snip + its add (either order); - `total` dropping to 0 is a fresh stew; num jumping to the stew (num = total) is a POUR; - `count` going up (Quest 5) is the code counting the digit it just peeked. A wrong solution is drawn as the code made it; captions say "Your code…" where it differs from the rule. Pure module (unit-tested); the component is components/replay/goblin-cauldron.tsx.

nodes.label: home-pull.ts
nodes.desc: Home, bulletin first: the world map is a pull-down shade wound up under the top bar. A strip of its torn bottom edge hangs below the roll so it reads as a map; the brass tab opens it over the bulletin (no dragging). Everything is measured as `rolled`: how far the sheet is wound up (0 = open, `closedRolled()` = wound up with only the strip showing). Pure functions so the gesture and the fall are unit-tested.

nodes.label: joust-scroll.ts
nodes.desc: The Royal Scroll (Tutorial Island · the Royal Joust): the replay scene's state, read from the real timeline. The scroll is a stack drawn newest-on-top; in Python it's a list whose END is the top (scroll[-1]). The runner records the player's own list (tracked names below) on every event and a `read` event for each call it takes from `operations` (or `shouts`), so each frame shows exactly what the player's code did after one call: a wrong combo shows the wrong number. Pure module (unit-tested); the component is components/replay/joust-scroll.tsx.

nodes.label: levels.ts
nodes.desc: Character level, derived from XP for display only (the server stores XP, not levels). Reaching level L takes 10·(L−1)·(L+4) XP: 60 for Lv 2, 140 for Lv 3, 240 for Lv 4. Clearing the whole Forest of Patience (300 XP) lands a new player in Lv 4.

nodes.label: masquerade-line.ts
nodes.desc: The Masquerade Line (Tutorial Island · the Masquerade Ball): the replay scene's state, read from the real timeline. The guests stand in one line, one letter-mask each (the string), and Lady Featherwhistle's tally book is the player's own dict (`book`, tracked by the runner). Strings don't record `read` events, so the frames come from the code's loops as the runner recorded them (line events carry vars as they were BEFORE the line ran): - pass 1 = the loop whose iterations change the book: one frame per guest, the book after that guest; - pass 2 = the next loop after it: one frame per guest looked up, `book[mask]` from the recorded book; - no book (e.g. looking only ahead with `s[i] not in s[i + 1:]`): one frame per guest the code stood at. The end frame draws what the code returned. Only there, and only when the answer is wrong, the true tallies point at the copy (decision 7a). Long lines fold (decision 8a, same 24 rule as the Spun Vault row) and pass 1 plays fast (decision 9a). Pure module (unit-tested); the component is components/replay/masquerade-line.tsx.

nodes.label: notebook-layout.ts
nodes.desc: Geometry for the floating Quest Notebook. The saved layout is fractions of the screen (synced across devices); on each device it becomes a pixel rectangle and is clamped so the notebook stays usable: never smaller than MIN_W × MIN_H, never larger than the screen, and at least GRAB px of the leather binding always on screen so it can be dragged back.

nodes.label: party-assist.ts
nodes.desc: Party Assist (C3b): during a running party questline, a player whose own quest is done (no unfinished claim) can join a teammate's unfinished quest in a shared live editor (the boss fight's CodeMirror 6 + Yjs relay). Rules, enforced by lib/party-assist-service.ts over both stores (migration 202610130001): - one room per claimed quest, at most MAX_HELPERS helpers; a helper is in one room at a time; - only the owner's Submit counts (through the normal /api/run path, with the shared code); helpers get no rewards for that quest and can't open its hints or solution (no hint penalty for the owner); - the shared doc starts from the owner's saved draft (else the quest's starter code); - the room ends when the owner clears the quest, the owner stops sharing, the questline ends or the party's lineup changes. A helper who claims a quest of their own drops out of the room. Browsers only see member row ids, never user ids.

nodes.label: party-boss.ts
nodes.desc: Party boss fight (C4): the party fights the region's boss together in one shared editor. - Ready room: once the party cleared every quest of the run, everyone gets a centred "boss gate is open" card. When every member presses Ready, the fight starts for everyone after a 3-2-1 (COUNTDOWN_MS). The leader can Start anyway (everyone enters, ready or not). A member not seen for OFFLINE_MS doesn't block: the ready players can vote to go in without them (they can still join from the toast later). Late joiners use the toast. The shared code is a Yjs document (Y.Text "code"), seeded with the boss's starter code. - Edits travel through the app server (server relay): browsers send Yjs updates + their awareness (cursor, name) every SYNC_MS; the server appends them to a log and pings `party:<id>` with an empty Realtime broadcast; the others fetch what's new. The server holds the document, so the code it grades is exactly what everyone sees. - Pings (👀 Look here, ✅ Done, ❓ Help) pin to the sender's cursor line for PING_MS. - C4b: everyone presses Submit on the current version (`head`); any edit after that resets every Submit. When every fighter has submitted the current version, the server grades its copy once. A fighter not seen for VOTE_AFTER_MS can be voted out by everyone still connected; they can rejoin until the boss falls. - Rewards: the clear counts in the leader's world; each fighter gets the boss rewards (XP, gold, Shard) once per player and boss, ever (solo clear or party reward). Hints/solution penalties apply only to whoever opened them.

nodes.desc: exports: getDraftService

nodes.label: party-draft-service.ts
nodes.desc: The lineup (server only, user ids): the boss store's party context.

nodes.label: party-draft-store.ts
nodes.desc: Party START draft storage: one draft per party (a JSON row; stage + round kept as columns for compare-and-set) and this round's picks. Local SQLite or Supabase tables (migration 202610110001, service_role only). The rules live in lib/party-draft.ts and lib/party-draft-service.ts.

nodes.label: party-draft.ts
nodes.desc: Party START draft (Eric's design): the leader presses START with ☝ Pick or ⇄ Shuffle. - Everyone sees 3 → 2 → 1 (COUNTDOWN_MS). - Pick: every player points at one of the region's quests (PICK_MS). You can move your hand until everyone has chosen or time runs out; anyone who hasn't chosen gets a random free quest. Two or more on the same quest: the server throws rock-paper-scissors for them until one wins. The winner gets the quest; if exactly one player and one quest are left, the loser gets it; otherwise the losers pick again among what's left (REPICK_MS). With 2 players one quest stays open: whoever finishes first can claim it. - Shuffle: quests are dealt at random. Then the questline starts (C3 claims) and each player's quest opens. All times are server times; the browser plays the countdown, clashes and the deal from them, so every screen shows the same thing.

nodes.label: party-store.ts
nodes.desc: Party storage (C2). Every call also counts as a heartbeat (presence) and tidies the caller's party (expired invites, lobby members offline too long). Results carry the Realtime topics to ping (lib/realtime.ts). `allowedRegions`: regions this player may pick as leader (the route works them out from their progress).

nodes.label: party.ts
nodes.desc: Parties (C2). Rules, enforced by both stores (lib/party-store.ts, migration 202610080001): - one party at a time, PARTY_SIZE seats; any member can invite an accepted friend (online or not); invites last INVITE_TTL_MS; joining another party leaves your current one; - the leader picks the region (any region the leader has discovered: members join the leader's world); if the leader leaves, the longest-standing member leads; the party ends when the last member leaves; - lobby members offline for LOBBY_DROP_MS are dropped, with a note to the others; - any change to the lineup clears everyone's READY; picking or changing the region keeps it (only START needs READY). - C3: when everyone's READY the leader STARTs the region's questline. Each member claims one quest at a time and solves it alone; the clear counts in the leader's world (leader's campaign), the solver gets the rewards (once per player and quest). Leaving releases your unfinished claims. The boss (together) is C4. Browsers only see party ids, member/invite row ids and their own inbox key, never user ids.

nodes.label: stairs-beats.ts
nodes.desc: Playback plan for the castle staircase (Eric's design): - Loop solutions: each loop step (a new stair computed by `a, b = b, a + b`) plays as four beats, Add → Slide → Forget → Store. Python evaluates the whole right side first, so Add comes before anything moves. The first two loop steps play slowly; later ones speed up. ~40 s at 1×. - Recursive solutions: a call tree where every knight is named after its call, ropes show each split, and answers climb back up to the caller. Everything is derived from the recorded run, so the animation still fails where the code fails.

nodes.label: stairs-replay.ts
nodes.desc: Turns a Climbing Stairs replay timeline into what the castle staircase shows at one cursor position. Everything here comes from the recorded run: step counts are the values the player's code actually held or returned, never recomputed answers. The true route counts (`ways`) are used only to mark the first step where the code went wrong, so the animation "fails where the code fails". Line events carry variables as they were *before* that line ran (Python's tracer), so a value written by line k shows up on the next event.

nodes.label: submit-moment.ts

A syntax error never ran anything: no animation, just the error mark. - Run keeps the case list first.

nodes.label: tutorial-island.ts
nodes.desc: Tutorial Island: a map category of its own for people who can't code yet, apart from the campaign chain (Forest → Vault → …). It holds several questline packs played in order (questline N+1 opens after questline N's boss) and optional side bosses that aren't needed to finish the island. The Forest is never locked behind it. A pack joins the island with a top-level `island` field: { "kind": "questline", "order": 4, "finale": true } questline 4, the island's last one (the only Shard) { "kind": "side", "after": 1 } optional side boss, opens after questline 1's boss Unlocks still live in content (`unlock.requiresQuestIds`, enforced by the server); tests/unit/tutorial-island.test.ts checks that the content matches the order here. Pure module (no JSON imports) so node unit tests can import it.

nodes.label: wobble-dance.ts
nodes.desc: The Dance Card (Tutorial Island · Sir Wobblesworth): the replay scene's state, read from the real timeline. The card is the string of steps (U/D/L/R); the village is a grid drawn like a maths graph, so U is y + 1 and goes UP the page, and his doormat is (0, 0). Every frame comes from recorded data: one loop pass of the player's code = one letter of the card, and where he stands is the player's own `x` / `y` (runner TRACKED_NAMES) after that pass, so a wrong walk is drawn as the code walked it. The end frame reads what the code RETURNED against where he really stands ("only x checked", "said True with steps still on the card"). The true answer is only used to say where it went wrong. Pure module (unit-tested); the component is components/replay/wobble-dance.tsx. Three shapes share the scene, picked from the case's arguments: - `walk`: a card to dance (`moves` for the boss, `path` for Q4): the whole walk, ending on the final tile. - `one`: Q3 `take_step(x, y, step)`: one step on the grid from the tile he was given. - `count`: Q1/Q2 (`card`, optional `letter`): the card only, letters the code counted lit.

nodes.label: quest_runner.py
nodes.desc: CPython execution and grading engine for Quest Coder. Submitted code is executed by ``execute_case`` and graded by ``run_one_case``. With ``isolate=True`` (what the CLI uses) every case executes in a separate worker process that receives only the source and the case inputs, so expected values and the verdict never share an interpreter with submitted code. The source checks and resource limits here are defense in depth. They are not an OS isolation boundary; the runner service must still be deployed in a locked-down container or microVM.

nodes.label: build_pack_projections.py

It keeps server-released solution and hint text plus public Run/replay cases, but never contains private Submit fixtures. `content/public/<slug>.json` removes solution and hint text before browser bundling. Private grading packs are mounted only by the runner and are deliberately not an input to this script. Run with `--check` to fail when public projections are stale.

nodes.label: copy_browser_runtime.mjs
nodes.desc: Copies what Run basic needs in the browser into public/ (gitignored; regenerated by predev/prebuild): public/pyodide/<version>/ Python for the browser, from the pinned `pyodide` npm package (served immutable) public/engine/ the grading engine shared with the runner + the Web Worker that drives it Nothing private goes here: the engine has no hidden tests or answers, and Run only uses public cases.

nodes.label: load_test_runner.ts
nodes.desc: S2 load test: simulated players Submit against the runner directly, in rising steps, so we can see where the runner starts to bend before it breaks. See docs/RUNNER_CAPACITY.md. RUNNER_URL=https://quest-coder-runner-staging-....run.app RUNNER_TOKEN=... node scripts/load_test_runner.ts Settings (environment): STAGES=50,200,500,1000,1500 players at each step (players are added, never removed, between steps) STAGE_SECONDS=180 how long each step runs INTERVAL_MIN_S=30 INTERVAL_MAX_S=60 each player waits a random time in this range between Submits PASS_SHARE=0.7 share of Submits that send the reference solution (the rest send starter code) OUT=path.json also write the full results as JSON It refuses any target that isn't localhost or a "staging" service, so real players are never load-tested. The token is read from the environment and never printed.

nodes.label: 202610020001_quest_coder_auth_progress.sql
nodes.desc: Quest Coder Supabase progress store. Idempotent: safe to re-run in the Supabase SQL editor or CLI migrations.

nodes.label: 202610040001_quest_coder_rewards_gold_skills.sql
nodes.desc: M5a rewards: Gold on every first clear and XP into the pack's skill (e.g. dynamic-programming). Replaces two functions from 202610020001; safe to apply more than once. Existing saves are not backfilled: past clears keep the XP and Shards they earned, and Gold/skills start at 0.

nodes.label: 202610050001_quest_coder_notebook_notes_layout.sql
nodes.desc: Pocket notebook: per-quest notes and the notebook's position/size, synced to the account. Adds one function next to quest_coder_merge_client_progress; safe to apply more than once. notes: { "<challengeId>": "text" }, at most 4000 characters each, at most 200 quests. notesVersions: per-quest revisions (same rule as savedCode): a save is accepted only when the browser's revision matches, so an old device can't overwrite newer notes. notebookLayout: { "x", "y", "w", "h" } as fractions of the screen, last write wins.

nodes.label: 202610060001_quest_coder_training_activity.sql
nodes.desc: Training activity: runs per day for the profile's streak and training calendar. Adds one function; safe to apply more than once. No new tables. activeDays: { "YYYY-MM-DD": <runs that day> } in the player's local date. The app checks the date is within a day of the server's date; this function also refuses anything further than two days from today. Only the newest 400 days are kept. Browsers can't write it (it is not part of the client merge).

nodes.label: 202610070001_quest_coder_friends.sql
nodes.desc: Friends (C1): friend codes, requests, friends list. Safe to apply more than once. Only the app server (service_role) touches these tables, through the functions below; browsers never read them directly. Rules match lib/friends.ts and the local store (lib/friends-store.ts): * a request goes out only by friend code and needs the other player to accept; * 10 request attempts per player per hour, wrong codes included (codes can't be guessed); * at most 100 friends + outgoing requests; * a declined request still shows to its sender as "sent" (nobody learns they were declined).

nodes.label: 202610080001_quest_coder_parties.sql
nodes.desc: Parties (C2): presence, parties, members, invites. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610070001 (friends). Same rules as lib/party.ts and the local store (lib/party-store.ts). Only the app server (service_role) calls quest_coder_party(); browsers never touch these tables. Every call is also a heartbeat. Realtime: the server pings `party:<party id>` / `inbox:<inbox key>` with an empty broadcast after changes; browsers then fetch the state again. Party ids and inbox keys are random and only given to the players concerned.

nodes.label: 202610090001_quest_coder_party_questline.sql
nodes.desc: Party questline (C3): START, quest claims, clears in the leader's world. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610080001 (parties). Same rules as lib/party-store.ts. service_role only. A campaign party plays in the leader's world: a member's clear moves the LEADER's campaign (no rewards for the leader), and the solver gets the rewards once per quest (their own campaign doesn't move).

nodes.label: 202610100001_quest_coder_party_boss.sql
nodes.desc: Party boss fight (C4): the shared editor's document log, fighters (presence, cursor, ping, Submit), votes. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610090001 (party questline). The app server reads and writes these tables with the service role (lib/party-boss-store.ts); browsers never do. party_boss_updates holds Yjs updates (base64), compacted by the server; the server rebuilds the code from them and grades exactly that.

nodes.label: 202610110001_quest_coder_party_draft.sql
nodes.desc: Party START draft: countdown, pick (or shuffle), rock-paper-scissors clashes, then the questline starts. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610100001 (party boss: its grants let the server read parties/members). The app server reads and writes these tables with the service role (lib/party-draft-store.ts); browsers never do. `data` holds the whole draft (lib/party-draft.ts DraftRow: players, assignments, clashes as user ids); stage + round are columns so a round is closed exactly once (compare-and-set).

nodes.label: 202610120001_quest_coder_party_region_keeps_ready.sql
nodes.desc: Picking or changing the party region keeps everyone's READY (only START needs everyone READY). Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610090001 (it replaces quest_coder_party_run, the wrapper the app calls). The base function (202610080001) still clears READY on a region change; the wrapper saves each member's READY before it runs the region action and puts it back afterwards, with a "<leader> changed the party region." notice. Lineup changes (join, leave, kick, offline drop) still clear READY.

nodes.label: 202610130001_quest_coder_party_assist.sql
nodes.desc: Party Assist: a player whose own quest is done joins a teammate's unfinished quest in a shared live editor. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610090001 (party questline) and 202610100001 (its grants let the server read parties, members and claims). The app server reads and writes these tables with the service role (lib/party-assist-store.ts); browsers never do. One room per claimed quest: party_assist_updates holds its Yjs updates (base64, compacted by the server). claimed_at/lineup record the owner's claim and the party lineup when the room opened: if either changes (quest cleared, questline ended, someone joined or left) the server ends the room.

nodes.label: 202610140001_quest_coder_start_choice.sql
nodes.desc: Tutorial Island: the first-login choice for new players ("island" = Tutorial Island, "forest" = jump right in). Adds one function; safe to apply more than once. No new tables, no new columns. startChoice lives in the progress payload next to the other server-owned fields. It is set once: a second call (another tab, a replayed request) returns the save unchanged. Browsers can't write it through quest_coder_merge_client_progress (that function only copies the fields it knows).

nodes.label: 202610150001_quest_coder_xp_floor_small_quests.sql
nodes.desc: Tutorial Island: small quests pay less than 5 XP (Questline 4, Quest 1 pays 4). The 5 XP floor on a clear (meant to keep help-assisted clears worth something) lifted a 4 XP quest to 5, so two quests paid the same and the questline total came out 1 XP high. The floor now never exceeds the quest's own base XP. Same change in both reward functions; everything else is copied unchanged from 202610040001 (apply_clear) and 202610090001 (grant_party_reward). Safe to apply more than once.

nodes.label: 202610160001_quest_coder_party_boss_gate.sql
nodes.desc: Party boss ready room: who has seen the open boss gate, who pressed Ready, who voted to go in without a member who's gone. Safe to apply more than once. Needs 202610100001 (party boss fight). The app server reads and writes this table with the service role (lib/party-boss-store.ts); browsers never do. A row only counts for the lineup + region it was written for and only after the run's latest claim (the server checks that on every read), so a new questline or a lineup change starts everyone at "not ready". Rows are deleted when the fight starts.
